summary: College week 3 is complete, all 75 games final, so this is the weekly review. Our number graded 71 of them. Two picks were published and went 1-1 for -0.05 units. The headline: our totals beat the closing line's own miss, our spreads did not.
weeklyReview: Against the closing spread, the side our number favoured went 36-34-1, 51.4%, under the 52.4% a -110 price needs to break even. On totals it went 41-30, 57.7%. That split is exactly what the calibration already assumes, which is why a college spread is shrunk almost to a coin flip and a total keeps a little more of its edge.

Average margin miss 10.9 points against the closing line's 9.52, so the market was still the better estimator of who wins by how much. On totals we were the closer of the two, 13.01 against 13.25. The old model, over the same slate, missed margins by 16.16.

Of the 54 games whose line moved after opening, it moved toward our number in 33, about 61%. That is the early signal that usually shows up before wins and losses do, and it is the one number this week that looks like an edge.
85% of finals landed inside our 80% range, so the ranges we publish are a touch wide rather than too confident.

Picks: Texas A&M -16.5 at -118 lost when Kentucky won outright 31-21; Duke -10 at -105 won 35-7. Both were sourced on injury reports and both were thin-sample reads, which is the honest description of every college number this early.

Of five model leans documented and passed on Saturday, four would have won. Five games is noise, not evidence, but the pattern is now on the record twice; if passing on totals after the market moves on news keeps costing, the rule is worth testing rather than assuming.
